metadata.title: Grade Classifier
metadata.description: Map a score from 0 to 100 to a letter grade with a single if/elif/else chain.

instructions.main: A student scored 70. Print the letter grade: 90+ is A, 80+ is B, 70+ is C, 60+ is D, anything lower is E.
steps: Use ONE chain: `if score >= 90: A`, `elif score >= 80: B`, `elif score >= 70: C`, `elif score >= 60: D`, `else: E`.
Print the grade. A score of exactly 70 must be a C.

hints.message: Build one chain: `if score >= 90` → A, `elif score >= 80` → B, `elif score >= 70` → C, `elif score >= 60` → D, `else` → E.
Separate `if` blocks all run, so a later one overwrites the grade — keep a single `if / elif / else` chain.
Use `>=` at the boundaries: a score of exactly 70 must be a C, not a D.
No `while` loop is needed here — classify the score with `if / elif / else`.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: The score is classified with one correct if/elif/else chain.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: A score of exactly 70 must print `C` — check your boundary comparisons.
Use one chain with at least three `elif` branches after the initial `if`.
